Despite these efforts, the threat of jihadism persists in neighboring countries like Mali and Burkina Faso, prompting concerns about porous borders and evolving tactics employed by groups like Al-Qaida-affiliated Jama’at Nusrat ul-Islam wa al-Muslimin (JNIM).

articles.title: June quarter earnings to determine market direction, says Sunil Subramaniam, warns on risks in near term - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Subramaniam, a financial expert, believes the recent rally in pharmaceuticals stocks was partly due to rupee depreciation and export-oriented companies. However, he cautions against extrapolating current quarterly earnings into the future as they don't fully reflect higher input costs. He expects consumer durables to outperform FMCG companies in the near term due to strong demand for products like air conditioners and refrigerators.  He also favors public sector banks over private lenders and believes the June quarter earnings season will be crucial in determining market direction.

articles.title: Even if the Iran war ended today, US fuel prices aren’t likely to normalize this year | Oil | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump faces backlash in polls due to rising gas prices, which have increased since the US and Israel attacked Iran. Experts say it will take several months, possibly years, for prices to return to prewar levels of about $3 a gallon because of damage to energy infrastructure and supply chain issues. While a peace deal could lead to initial price drops, industry experts estimate recovery time could range from six months to two years due to the complexities of restoring oil production and transportation in the Persian Gulf.  The war's impact on fuel prices is likely to remain volatile as long as hostilities continue.

articles.title: Government plans to inaugurate Bhogapuram Airport on July 5: MP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: M. Sribharat, an MP, announced that the State government plans to inaugurate the International Airport at Bhogapuram on July 5th with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.  He expressed confidence that several airlines would soon begin operations from the new airport following its inauguration. Scoot Airlines will commence international services from Bhogapuram Airport starting July 8th.

articles.title: Bitcoin faces fresh selling pressure despite U.S.-Iran easing; over $400 million liquidated in 1 day - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bitcoin and Ethereum experienced weekly declines, falling 4.31% and 7.15%, respectively, due to global macroeconomic concerns like rising Treasury yields and persistent inflation. The broader risk-off environment led to outflows from crypto investment products, with Bitcoin funds accounting for the majority of withdrawals.  Piyush Walke, a Derivatives Research Analyst at Delta Exchange, stated that easing U.S.-Iran tensions failed to revive sentiment in the market, while continued outflows from Bitcoin ETFs and profit-taking after a U.S. Senate crypto bill breakthrough kept pressure on digital assets.

articles.title: As Salah plays final Liverpool match, his legacy goes far beyond the pitch | Football | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mohamed Salah, a 33-year-old Egyptian forward, will play his final match for Liverpool this Sunday.  His legacy extends far beyond the pitch as he has become a cultural icon with a lasting impact on fans and aspiring players alike.  He is one of the greatest Liverpool players of all time, boasting numerous accolades including two Premier League titles and four league Golden Boots. Salah's authenticity in embracing his Muslim faith and North African heritage has challenged stereotypes and inspired others to embrace their own identities.

articles.title: Democratic chair faces calls to quit over ‘shambles’ of election autopsy release | Democrats | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ken Martin, chair of the Democratic National Committee (DNC), faces calls to resign following the release of a flawed autopsy report on the 2024 presidential election. The report, which omitted key information and lacked oversight, has deepened concerns about Martin's leadership and sparked criticism from Democratic members of Congress and party leaders.  Several voices have called for his resignation, including Seth Moulton, Marc Veasey, and Mark Pocan.  Norm Solomon and Amanda Litman also expressed their dissatisfaction with the report and Martin's handling of it. The Progressive Change Campaign Committee (PCCC) has launched a campaign to pressure state chairs to call for Martin's resignation, while others have suggested potential successors like Jane Kleeb and Ben Wikler.

articles.title: Back Rahul Gandhi’s call for ‘Samvidhan Bachao’, says Jagga Reddy - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: T. Jagga Reddy, a senior Congress leader, defended Rahul Gandhi's "Samvidhan Bachao" campaign, arguing that the Constitution and democratic values are under threat under the current BJP-led government. He compared the Constitution to Karna's armor in the Mahabharata, stating that its protection is vital for citizens' rights and freedoms.  He called for vigilance to safeguard voting rights and constitutional freedoms, highlighting Congress contributions to India's democratic systems throughout history.

articles.title: Gokaldas Exports posts 9% sequential rise in Q4 revenue - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Gokaldas Exports reported a lower profit for the fiscal year 2026 compared to the previous year, despite a 9% quarter-on-quarter increase in total income. The company attributed this growth to a recovery in its Africa business and steady performance in India, despite tariff disruptions. Sivaramakrishnan Ganapathi, vice chairman and managing director of Gokaldas Exports, highlighted the impact of US tariffs and geopolitical events on costs and margins, but emphasized the company's resilience and strong customer relationships.

articles.title: Missiles to munitions: Does the US risk running out of key weapons? | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US Navy secretary, Hung Cao, stated that the pause in weapons sales to Taiwan is not due to a critical shortage of weapons but rather to ensure sufficient munitions for the ongoing Iran war.  While officials project confidence in their stockpiles, analysts suggest dwindling munitions may influence Washington's calculations regarding resuming the war on Iran. The Pentagon and Israel defended their joint strategy of interceptor deployments, downplaying concerns about depleted weapons. However, a report by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) revealed that the US heavily used critical ammunitions like THAAD interceptors, Patriot missiles, and SM-3/SM-6 surface-to-air missiles during the Iran war.  The CSIS report also stated that rebuilding to pre-war levels for these munitions could take from one to four years. The depletion of these weapons has raised concerns among US allies in Asia, particularly Japan and South Korea, who rely on Washington as a deterrent against potential threats from North Korea and China.

articles.title: UK’s ‘anxious generation’ of young people struggling to adapt to workplace | Young people | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Alan Milburn, a former Labour health secretary, will release a report this week highlighting the struggles of young people in adapting to the current job market.  His review, commissioned by Prime Minister Keir Starmer, suggests that a rising tide of mental health issues and social media's influence are contributing factors to high economic inactivity among young adults. The report emphasizes that these young people face unique challenges due to their digital-native upbringing and calls for businesses to offer more flexibility and mental health support to address this issue.  This is expected to impact the government's approach to attracting skilled labor amid falling immigration rates.

articles.title: Toddler recovers after month-long critical care battle at Bengaluru hospital following road accident - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A one-year-nine-month-old child, Vihaan S. Jithin, suffered severe brain and lung injuries following a road accident in Bengaluru.  Doctors at Manipal Hospital Yelahanka treated the child for nearly a month, addressing multiple life-threatening complications including multidrug-resistant infection, aspiration-related lung injury, and neurological damage. The doctors used a combination of mechanical ventilation, bronchoscopy, targeted antimicrobial therapy, and rehabilitation to help Vihaan regain breathing, eating, and walking abilities.  The child was eventually discharged after 30 days in intensive care.

articles.title: NTPC Q4 Results: Cons PAT jumps 34% YoY to Rs 10,615 crore; Rs 3.5/share dividend announced - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The state-run power company's board recommended a final dividend of Rs 3.50 per share for the financial year 2025-26, subject to shareholder approval at the upcoming AGM. The company reported a significant increase in PAT (profit after tax) and revenue during Q4FY26, with revenues reaching Rs 48,548 crore compared to Rs 44,658 crore in Q3FY26.  The company's expenses also increased by 9% on a quarter-on-quarter basis but declined by 0.35% year-on-year.

articles.title: Aga Khan urges unity, education and service to humanity - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: His Highness Prince Rahim Al Hussaini Aga Khan V, the 50th spiritual leader of the Ismaili community, visited Gilgit-Baltistan on Friday. During his address to a large gathering in Passu, he emphasized the importance of unity, education, and faith within families and communities. Prince Rahim also encouraged young people to prepare for the future with confidence and awareness, urging them to seek global understanding and embrace English language learning. He stressed that Allah's guidance is always present and reminded community members to find peace through prayer and faith.

articles.title: Mexico beat Ghana as World Cup cohosts excel despite FIFA sanctions | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Mexico defeated Ghana 2-0 in a World Cup warm-up match in Puebla, despite FIFA sanctions limiting spectator capacity at the stadium.  Javier Aguirre, Mexico's coach, praised the performance of players vying for spots on the final World Cup squad, including Luis Chavez, Edson Alvarez, and Jorge Sanchez. The victory showcased the excitement building ahead of the tournament, which begins less than three weeks from now.

articles.title: ‘I don’t have a life’: man sent to France in ‘one in, one out’ refugee scheme tells of return to UK | Immigration and asylum | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: An asylum seeker who was returned to France under the UK's "one in, one out" scheme has secretly returned to Britain and is now living in hiding. The man told the Guardian he was aware of at least 18 other returnees who have also been returning clandestinely to the UK.  The Home Office insists anyone attempting to return after being deported under this agreement will be removed again, while organizations like the Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants argue that the government's border regime is pushing people into unsafe routes and criminalizing those seeking safety.

articles.title: Inside China’s 113-metre deep undersea tunnel: How a mega rail project could rewrite high-speed travel | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Engineers are constructing a high-speed rail tunnel beneath the Pearl River Estuary in southern China, a project that is pushing technological boundaries and reshaping how entire cities may soon connect.  The Shenzhen–Jiangmen high-speed rail project involves a large tunnel boring machine designed for deep undersea conditions, which is working to carve through unstable ground with layers of earth changing character without warning. The tunnel reaches depths exceeding 113 meters and will eventually link manufacturing hubs, ports, and major cities, reducing travel times across the Pearl River Delta.  The project underscores China's commitment to expanding its rail system into challenging terrain, particularly underwater zones previously requiring ferries or long detours.

articles.title: Chief Electoral Officer (Kerala) Rathan U. Kelkar appointed Secretary to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rathan U. Kelkar, the Chief Electoral Officer of Kerala, will transition from his role to become the Secretary to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan.  Mr. Kelkar, a 2003 batch IAS officer, has been in the news for overseeing the recent Kerala Assembly elections and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The appointment follows the recent appointment of Manoj Kumar Agarwal as Chief Secretary to the new BJP government in West Bengal.  The State government will send a panel of names to the Election Commission to appoint a new CEO once Mr. Kelkar is relieved of his duties.

articles.title: Bandhan Small Cap among top 5 smallcap funds with highest risk-adjusted returns. Check details - Risk adjusted returns | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Bandhan Small Cap Fund, ITI Small Cap Fund, and Aditya Birla Sun Life Smallcap 50 Index Fund were among the top performers in terms of Sharpe ratio, with returns exceeding risk-free rates.  The Bandhan Small Cap Fund led the pack with a ratio of 1.17 over the past three years, followed by ITI Small Cap Fund at 1.02 and Aditya Birla Sun Life Smallcap 50 Index Fund at 0.84.  Kotak Nifty Smallcap 50 Index Fund and Invesco India Smallcap Fund also showed positive returns with Sharpe ratios of 0.84 and 0.98 respectively.

articles.title: KP announces four Eid holidays from May 26 to 29 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Sindh, and federal governments have announced holidays for Eidul Azha. The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government declared four days of holiday from May 26 to May 29, while Sindh also announced a four-day holiday including Friday.  The federal government declared a three-day public holiday from May 26-28. Eidul Azha will be celebrated across Pakistan from May 27 to May 29.

articles.title: Man Utd’s Fernandes trumps Arsenal to Premier League player of season award | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Bruno Fernandes of Manchester United has been named the Premier League player of the season, earning the award after a strong campaign that saw him tie the league's assists record.  He scored eight goals and created 132 chances for his team, which secured third place in the standings and Champions League qualification. The Portuguese midfielder was nominated alongside other top players from Arsenal, Man City, and other clubs, but ultimately emerged as the standout performer of the season.

articles.title: ‘You can’t control everything’: the rise in plastic surgeons asked to create ‘AI face’ | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Dr. Nora Nugent, president of the British Association of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons, and Dr. Alex Karidis are observing a rise in clients seeking cosmetic surgery based on unrealistic AI-generated images.  These clients often demand procedures that are impossible to achieve through surgery alone, highlighting concerns about the influence of AI on aesthetic ideals and the potential for misleading information.  Surgeons warn against relying solely on these images as they fail to reflect the complexities of human anatomy and healing processes.

articles.title: 'Fast-developing emergency': 1 killed, several injured after fire, explosions at New York City Shipyard - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A fire at a shipyard in New York City on Friday resulted in one fatality and injuries to at least 36 people, including firefighters and first responders. Fire Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore and Chief of Department John Esposito described the incident as a complex emergency with multiple explosions occurring during firefighting efforts. The injured firefighter and fire marshal are currently under medical observation.  The cause of the fire is still under investigation.

articles.title: Organisations and environmentalists demand withdrawal of CJI’s remarks on activists - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: 49 organizations, collectives, and 553 environmentalists, academics, and citizens wrote a letter to the Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant demanding that he withdraw his oral remarks from May 11th. The letter argues that the CJI's comments were factually inaccurate, constitutionally troubling, and potentially dangerous, as they cast doubt on the legitimacy of environmental Public Interest Litigation (PIL).  The letter calls for courts to recognize citizens seeking lawful scrutiny of environmental decisions as rights-bearing participants in environmental decision-making rather than obstacles.

articles.title: Planning to take international exposure for three years? Here are top 5 global funds with over 40% gain - International gains | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nippon India Taiwan Equity Fund, Mirae Asset NYSE FANG+ ETF FoF, and DSP World Gold Mining Overseas Equity Omni FoF were among the top-performing funds in the last three years, according to MF Screener.  The Nippon India Taiwan Equity Fund led with a 64.14% return over three years, followed by Mirae Asset NYSE FANG+ ETF FoF at 51.09%.  Other top performers include DSP World Gold Mining Overseas Equity Omni FoF, and Motilal Oswal Nasdaq 100 FoF.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz lands in Hangzhou, kicking off 4-day China visit - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif arrived in Hangzhou, China, for a four-day official visit to commemorate the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and China.  He was welcomed by Vice Governor Xu Wenguang, China’s Ambassador Jiang Zaidong, and Islamabad’s envoy Khalil Hashmi. During his stay in Hangzhou, Shehbaz Sharif will attend a business forum focused on promoting cooperation between Pakistani and Chinese companies under the second phase of China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC 2.0). He will also meet with Zhejiang Party Secretary Wang Hao and engage with CEOs of leading Chinese companies, including a visit to Alibaba Group headquarters.  The visit is expected to strengthen political trust, strategic coordination, and expand practical cooperation between Pakistan and China.

articles.title: Uganda confirms three new Ebola cases, bringing total to five | Ebola News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Uganda's Ministry of Health confirmed three new Ebola cases, bringing the total number of infections to five. The new cases include a driver who transported the country’s first confirmed patient and a health worker exposed while caring for that patient.  The WHO has revised its risk assessment for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola to "very high" at the national level, "high" at the regional level, and "low" at the global level. The outbreak is centered in Democratic Republic of the Congo, where nearly 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths have been recorded.  The WHO is working with partners to contain the outbreak and support affected people.

articles.title: ‘Canada is handing people over to ICE’: refugees rejected at border face US detention | Canada | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Markens Appolon, a 25-year-old Haitian refugee, is detained in an ICE facility after being turned over to US authorities by Canadian officials.  Appolon sought asylum in Canada believing it offered a haven for those at risk but was rejected and now faces the consequences of his situation.  Canadian immigration lawyers say they are seeing an increase in cases like Appolon's since Donald Trump's second term began, citing concerns about the tightening of Canada's asylum system and the country's adherence to the Safe Third Country Agreement with the US. Erin Simpson, a Toronto-based immigration lawyer representing Appolon, argues that Canada is participating in this by handing refugees over to ICE.  The situation has led to increased scrutiny of Canada's asylum system and its approach to refugee claims.

articles.title: Experts urge hydration, awareness to prevent heat-related illnesses - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Experts at a webinar organized by The Hindu warned against delaying water consumption during extreme summer conditions, as symptoms like dizziness and excessive sweating can indicate serious heat-related illnesses.  Dr. Jaichitra Suresh, senior consultant physician and diabetologist at Soukya Clinic and Home Healthcare, and Dr. Karthik Gunasekaran, professor in the Department of General Medicine at Christian Medical College (CMC), Vellore, discussed the impact of rising temperatures on public health. They emphasized staying hydrated, avoiding direct sunlight during peak hours, wearing light-colored clothing, and reducing strenuous activity to prevent heat-related illnesses.

articles.title: PPFAS Mutual Fund introduces choti SIP in Parag Parikh Flexi Cap, Large Cap and 3 other schemes - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Parag Parikh Mutual Fund has introduced a new "Choti SIP" facility for its five equity funds, allowing first-time investors to invest in mutual funds with a minimum of Rs 250 per installment.  The fund house also announced changes to the Systematic Transfer Plan (STP) processing frequency, effective May 21, 2026, to only process on business days. The changes are part of an addendum to the Statement of Additional Information (SAI) and Scheme Information Documents (SIDs) for the affected schemes.

articles.title: 'A long-term strategic failure': Three months in, is Trump losing the war on Iran? - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump faces growing doubts about the success of his military campaign against Iran, despite initial tactical victories.  Analysts argue that the conflict has morphed into a protracted strategic failure, with Iran's resilience and continued support for proxy groups posing significant challenges to US objectives. While Trump maintains control over options on the table, he faces domestic pressure over rising gasoline prices and low approval ratings, making his position increasingly precarious. The crisis continues with no clear path to resolution, leaving experts predicting a grim post-war outlook for Trump.

articles.title: Israel attacks southern Lebanon and near Syrian border despite ‘ceasefire’ | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel launched new air strikes in Lebanon on Saturday, targeting areas near the Syrian border and several villages in southern Lebanon.  The attacks followed earlier raids that killed 10 people and came despite a ceasefire announced by President Donald Trump on April 16. The attacks have caused widespread displacement and fear among residents, with many fleeing their homes due to forced evacuation orders issued by Israel's military.  Lebanon’s Health Ministry reported over 3,100 deaths since the escalation of Israeli attacks in March.

articles.title: Fraudster trying to sell fake ancient statues to Sotheby’s foiled over bogus invoices | Crime | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Andrew Crowley, 46, was sentenced to a two-year suspended sentence for attempting to defraud Sotheby’s by selling fake ancient statues.  Crowley presented forged invoices claiming the statues were from 1976 and used printing methods that were 25 years too modern. Forensic analysis revealed the documents were fabricated, and the judge acknowledged Crowley did not intend to deceive but instead believed he inherited the items legitimately. Sotheby’s experts identified inconsistencies in the paperwork early on, preventing a potential fraud.

articles.title: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio four-day India visit updates - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in New Delhi on Saturday (May 23, 2026) for his first official visit to India, aiming to recalibrate bilateral relations that have faced headwinds since mid-last year.  He met with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and attended a meeting of the Quad Foreign Ministers. The trip comes after a period of strain between the two countries following trade disputes and President Donald Trump's statements regarding the India-Pakistan conflict.  The visit will focus on strengthening ties in areas such as energy, trade, investment, technology, and people-to-people exchanges, with discussions also expected to cover the West Asia crisis and its economic impact.

articles.title: London stabbing: Five men rushed to hospital after violent altercation, one arrested - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Five men were injured in a stabbing incident on Horn Lane in Acton, London, after a violent altercation.  Metropolitan Police responded to reports of multiple men being assaulted and stabbed at around 2:47 pm, with all five victims taken to the hospital. A suspect, aged 26, was arrested for grievous bodily harm (GBH) and drug possession. London Ambulance Service dispatched multiple emergency teams to the scene.  Police are investigating the incident and have increased security in the area.

articles.title: Nifty stays range-bound as resistance near 23,800 caps upside move - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The India VIX cooled off, declining 4.68% to 17.91 for the week. The Nifty index closed with a net gain of 75.80 points (+0.32%), but remains below a crucial resistance zone near 23,800-23,850.  While recent volatility has stabilized, traders should monitor the index's behavior near this level and avoid aggressive buying until it decisively breaks above. The Nifty Metal Index is showing relative strength, while other sectors like Midcap 100 and Energy are also performing well.

articles.title: Govt reduces petrol, high-speed diesel prices by Rs6 - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The government reduced the price of petrol by Rs6 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs6.80 on Friday, bringing the price of petrol to Rs403.78 per litre and HSD to Rs402.78. The Petroleum Division announced the new prices would be effective from May 23rd, marking the second consecutive week of fuel price reductions.  This decision comes after a period of fluctuating prices following the US-Israeli war on Iran in February. The government has been adjusting petroleum prices weekly since then, aiming to balance global market fluctuations and domestic needs.

articles.title: Kohli refuses Head handshake after heated Hyderabad-Bengaluru clash in IPL | Cricket News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Virat Kohli of Royal Challengers Bengaluru refused to shake hands with Travis Head of Sunrisers Hyderabad after their team's defeat in the Indian Premier League. The heated exchange occurred during the match, where Kohli was visibly angry and gestured towards Head to bowl. Despite a 55-run loss for Bengaluru, both teams have qualified for the IPL playoffs.

articles.title: UK, German and French aid cuts will take ‘devastating toll’ on most vulnerable, says study | Global development | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A new report by the Barcelona Institute for Global Health (ISGlobal) warns that cuts to foreign aid budgets by the UK, France, and Germany could contribute to over 11.5 million preventable deaths by the end of the decade. The report estimates that UK cuts alone could result in 5.1 million additional deaths by 2030, while France's reductions could lead to 3.5 million and Germany's to almost 2.9 million. The report highlights the detrimental impact of these cuts on global health systems, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, and emphasizes the need for predictable and multi-sourced financing to ensure a robust international system.

articles.title: Delhi Police files supplementary chargesheet in Parliament breach case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Delhi Police Special Cell filed a nearly 14,000-page supplementary chargesheet against the accused in the 2023 Parliament security breach case. The chargesheet, submitted before the Patiala House Court, includes allegations of terrorist acts, criminal conspiracy, and provocation to cause riots under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).  The prosecution argued that the filing was appropriate given ongoing proceedings on framing of charges, while defense counsel objected, arguing it was an abuse of process. The court directed a hard copy be supplied to the defense counsel and listed the matter for further scrutiny on May 29th.

articles.title: The Nile’s hidden shift over 4,000 years may have saved an entire ancient African city and preserved Napata for thousands of years | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Archaeologists from the University of Michigan, along with researchers in Sudan, have uncovered evidence suggesting that the Nile River played a crucial role in the longevity of the ancient city of Napata.  By analyzing sediment cores and studying the river's changing dynamics over thousands of years, they found that the Nile initially eroded the valley before gradually depositing fertile clay and silt around Napata. This gradual accumulation created a stable floodplain, reducing flooding while maintaining water for farming and settlement. The researchers believe this slow environmental shift may have been key to Napata's survival compared to other settlements in the region.  The findings shed light on the hidden role of the Nile in shaping ancient Nubian history and offer new insights into the Kingdom of Kush's expansion.

articles.title: FIIs sell over Rs 30K crore worth of Indian equities in May as outflows swell to Rs 2.22 lakh crore. What lies ahead? - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) sold domestic shares worth Rs 4,440.47 crore on Friday while domestic institutional investors (DIIs) were net buyers at Rs 6,003.53 crore. This helped the benchmark indices close with gains despite strong selling pressure in pharma and health stocks.  Pabitro Mukherjee, Associate Vice President - Research at Bajaj Broking, noted that investor sentiment remains cautious due to geopolitical tensions and rising interest rates. He added that institutional activity is expected to be driven by global developments, particularly US-Iran negotiations.

articles.title: Passengers safely evacuated after Metro bus catches fire in Pindi - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A Metro bus caught fire near the 6th Road stop in Rawalpindi on Saturday morning, causing significant damage but no injuries.  Rescue officials extinguished the blaze and suspended service between Rawalpindi and Islamabad. The cause of the fire is still under investigation. This incident follows similar incidents in Lahore where passengers were injured or a bus was completely burnt due to fires.

articles.title: Zelenskyy says ‘time is right’ for Ukraine to start process of joining EU | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Zelenskyy, the Ukrainian President, has called for the initiation of Ukraine's accession to the European Union, arguing that associate membership would be unfair and limit Kyiv's ability to advance its interests.  He emphasized that Ukraine's efforts to join the EU have intensified following Hungary's former prime minister, Viktor Orban, being ousted in parliamentary elections last month.  Zelenskyy also highlighted recent Ukrainian military successes, including retaking significant territory from Russia and inflicting heavy casualties on Russian troops. The UN has expressed concern over reports of a drone attack in Luhansk that resulted in civilian casualties, while Zelenskyy reported attacks on Russian oil infrastructure and military facilities.

articles.title: Pope meets families who lost children to toxic waste in Italy’s ‘Land of Fires’ | Italy | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Pope Leo XIV visited the Terra dei Fuochi, a region near Naples, to express condolences to families who lost loved ones due to illegal toxic dumping. The visit coincided with the 11th anniversary of Pope Francis’s encyclical *Laudato Si*, highlighting the pontiff's commitment to environmental issues. The European Court of Human Rights last year validated residents' complaints about the mafia-run waste disposal that led to increased cancer rates in the area, prompting Italy to establish a database and address health risks. Pope Leo XIV urged those responsible for the pollution to repent and called on authorities to heal the land, emphasizing the suffering inflicted upon generations of people.

articles.title: Financial decisions will rest with elected leaders: Sonam Wangchuk on Ladakh’s agreement with Centre - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sonam Wangchuk, a renowned climate activist, welcomed the agreement between the Centre and representatives of Ladakh Apex Body (LAB) and Kargil Democratic Alliance (KDA) which will see an elected Chief Minister for the Union Territory of Ladakh.  The decision grants the UT-level Assembly legislative power over budget allocation and bureaucracy control, with the elected representatives taking responsibility for financial decisions. The agreement also includes safeguards under Article 371 to protect environment, land, culture, and nature.

articles.title: Uganda confirms 3 new Ebola cases as WHO warns against underestimating outbreak risk - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Uganda's health ministry confirmed three new Ebola cases, bringing the total to five in the country. The new infections include a driver and a health worker who were exposed to the first confirmed patient, as well as a woman from the Democratic Republic of Congo who entered Uganda with symptoms.  The World Health Organization (WHO) has declared the outbreak a public health emergency of international concern due to its potential for spreading beyond Congo and Uganda. The WHO Africa director warned against underestimating the outbreak's severity, emphasizing the lack of a vaccine for the Bundibugyo strain.

articles.title: PM Shehbaz lands in China on 4-day visit - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif arrived in China on Saturday for a four-day official visit, accompanied by several high-ranking officials. The trip coincides with the 75th anniversary of Pakistan and China's diplomatic relations and will focus on strengthening bilateral cooperation across various sectors, including trade, investment, and people-to-people exchanges. Shehbaz Sharif is scheduled to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Premier Li Qiang, discussing key areas like the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) development and regional security issues, particularly the US-Iran war.

articles.title: Senegal’s President Faye sacks PM Sonko and dissolves government | News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Senegal’s President Bassirou Diomaye Faye dismissed Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko and dissolved the government, a move that could further delay negotiations with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).  The decision follows months of growing tensions between Faye and Sonko, who had been allies but became increasingly estranged. The IMF froze a $1.8 billion lending program following misreported debt discovered by the previous government, pushing Senegal's debt level to 132 percent of its economic output.  Sonko, a popular opposition leader, is now unclear on his next steps after being removed from his position as Prime Minister.

articles.title: UK needs ‘national consensus’ over rejoining EU, David Miliband says | David Miliband | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: David Miliband, president of the International Rescue Committee, believes that Britain needs a national consensus on its relationship with the European Union. He argues for a "much higher dosage" in the UK's reset with Europe than currently planned.  He acknowledges the changing landscape of the EU, particularly the increasing importance of Ukraine and the need to address issues like wealth creation and government reform.

articles.title: ‘I will kill you Jews’: Man jailed for 5 years in UK over antisemitic threats near London synagogue - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A London court sentenced Tavius Jean-Charles, a 36-year-old man, to five years in prison for seven racially aggravated public order offences and one count of racially aggravated criminal damage.  Jean-Charles targeted six Jewish victims in Stamford Hill between October 2025 and March 2026, including shouting death threats at synagogue manager Barry Bard and threatening another resident, Joel Scher. He was arrested after witnesses reported his repeated death threats near synagogues, and later made a statement about blowing up Jewish schools. The case highlights the rising concern over antisemitic attacks in the UK, with authorities pledging to address hate crimes more swiftly.

articles.title: Reliance Industries, TCS, among 10 stocks with sharpest decrease in retail shareholding in Q4 - Retail holding decline | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Rising oil prices and geopolitical tensions in the Iran war have contributed to a decline in investor confidence, leading to decreased retail holdings across several Indian companies.  HDFC Bank, Reliance Industries, ITC, Larsen & Toubro, Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, Jio Financial Services, Hindustan Unilever, and Asian Paints all saw significant drops in retail shareholding during the March quarter, with some stocks experiencing declines of over 20%.  This trend reflects a broader market sentiment of caution as investors grapple with rising inflation and potential interest rate hikes.

articles.title: ‘Ukraine needs to win this war’: Iceland PM says India and Nordics have different views on Russia, but common cause with peace - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Iceland’s Prime Minister Kristrún Mjöll Frostadóttir expressed hopes for increased bilateral trade between India and the Nordic countries, particularly in renewable energy technologies.  She also advocated for more Indian films to be shot in Iceland, during her visit to the India-Nordic Summit in Oslo on Tuesday (May 19, 2026). The summit aimed to foster cooperation among middle powers amidst concerns about global power dynamics.

articles.title: 12 terrorists killed, one person dead in heavy fighting between police, militants in KP's Bannu - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A police peace committee and militants clashed in Bannu district, resulting in the deaths of at least 12 terrorists and one police officer.  The incident occurred during heavy fighting that saw four policemen injured. The deceased was a retired personnel of the Federal Constabulary.  Following the clashes, additional reinforcements were called to the area. Bannu police also successfully defused a 10-kilogramme remote-controlled bomb near a mosque in Mamash Khel. This incident comes amid a resurgence of terrorism in Pakistan, particularly in KP and Balochistan, since the return of the Taliban to power in Afghanistan.

articles.title: Iran weighs US peace proposal despite ‘deep and significant’ disagreements | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan’s army chief, Asim Munir, met with Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Tehran, signaling progress in peace talks.  Despite the visit and diplomatic efforts by Pakistan’s Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, who are mediating between the warring sides, Iran insists on deep disagreements remaining. The US has also expressed its readiness for strikes if negotiations fail.

articles.title: Reeves begins push to remain as chancellor under new Labour leadership | Rachel Reeves | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rachel Reeves, the UK chancellor, is facing pressure to stay in her position despite calls for a new leader within Labour.  Her supporters argue that she is the best candidate to maintain financial stability and reassure markets. However, concerns remain about her ability to address the new economic challenges posed by the Iran war and potential changes under a new prime minister, particularly given the possibility of Andy Burnham replacing Keir Starmer. Reeves has been actively lobbying MPs to support her candidacy, but some Labour MPs are critical of her handling of issues like winter fuel payments and disability benefits.  The future of the chancellor's job remains uncertain as she navigates these internal challenges.

articles.title: World’s most powerful economies by 2030: Prediction reveals future global leaders | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: By 2030, several emerging economies are projected to rise in global GDP rankings, while established industrial powers may experience slight declines. China is expected to remain the world's largest economy by purchasing power parity measures, driven by its manufacturing scale and increasing focus on technology, infrastructure investment, and consumer spending. The United States, despite competition from Asia, is predicted to maintain a top tier position due to financial markets, research institutions, multinational companies, and the continued influence of the US dollar.  India, Japan, Germany, Russia, Indonesia, Brazil, United Kingdom, and France are also expected to remain influential in the global economy.

articles.title: Nomura picks 6 stocks with up to 49% upside potential that can benefit from India’s EV push - EV Boost | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Nomura, an international brokerage, predicts a surge in India's electric vehicle (EV) adoption due to government policies and rising fuel prices. The brokerage recommends six stocks likely to benefit from this trend: Mahindra & Mahindra, Hyundai Motor India, TVS Motors, Ather Energy, Sona BLW Precision Forgings, and UNO Minda. These companies are expected to see significant growth in the near future, with potential upside ranging from 20% to 49%.

articles.title: Chennai and neighbouring areas to get light to moderate rains over the weekend - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chennai experienced a hot Friday with temperatures reaching 40.8 degrees Celsius at Meenambakkam and 39.8 degrees Celsius at Nungambakkam, but the city woke up to cooler conditions on Saturday due to the early onset of moisture-bearing Easterlies. The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) has issued a Nowcast bulletin predicting light to moderate rain over several districts in Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, with the possibility of heavy rain accompanied by thunderstorms and gusty winds in some areas.  The RMC also forecasts heavy rain and thunderstorms in isolated places across various districts of Tamil Nadu and neighboring regions on Sunday.

articles.title: Inquiry panel at Multan hospital finds 9 doctors, officials at fault for surgery conducted sans HIV screening - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Nishtar Medical University has found nine doctors and hospital officials guilty of misconduct and violation of screening protocols in a case involving surgery on an HIV-positive patient, prompting disciplinary action by the Punjab government.  The inquiry committee recommended disciplinary proceedings under the Punjab Employees Efficiency, Discipline and Accountability (Peeda) Act 2006. The Punjab health department suspended several officials, including Dr Fariha Ahmed, Rida Zahra, and others for incompetence and mismanagement.  The incident has raised concerns about compliance with infection-control protocols at the hospital.

articles.title: North Korean women’s team win Asian Champions League title in South Korea | Sport News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Naegohyang Women’s FC, a North Korean women's football team, won the Asian Champions League title in South Korea after defeating Tokyo Verdy Beleza 1-0. This victory marks the first time a North Korean sports team has visited the South in eight years and earns them a spot in next year’s FIFA Women’s Champions Cup. The final was played at Suwon Stadium in front of a mixed crowd of South Korean spectators, with many expressing hope that this event can contribute to easing tensions between the two countries.

articles.title: Reeves’s tax cut on children’s meals a political ‘soundbite’, say restaurateurs | Tax and spending | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Rachel Reeves, the chancellor, announced a temporary reduction in VAT on children’s meals in restaurants from 20% to 5% between June and September. Will Murray, owner of London restaurant Fallow, and Tim Martin, founder and chair of Wetherspoons, have expressed skepticism about the impact of the measure, arguing that it won't make a significant difference for families or businesses.  UKHospitality, the lobbying group for the industry, has called for a permanent reduction in VAT for the entire hospitality sector to bring the UK in line with European rates.

articles.title: King Charles Iii: King Charles surprises audience at Kenneth Branagh’s sold-out Shakespeare show in Stratford-upon-Avon | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: King Charles III surprised audiences at a sold-out performance of The Tempest at the Royal Shakespeare Company's Royal Shakespeare Theatre in Stratford-upon-Avon. The King, who became patron of the company in 2024, sat among ordinary audience members and was greeted with applause as he took his seat between Daniel Evans and Tamara Harvey, the co-artistic directors.  The appearance, which was kept secret, added to the excitement surrounding the production starring Kenneth Branagh, who is making his first performance in the iconic Shakespeare role. The play has been a major attraction for audiences this season, with many describing the experience as "surreal" and "unforgettable".

articles.title: Contrarian Tactics: How to survive market volatility and generate steady returns - Investing approach | The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Michael Price, a renowned investing legend, advises investors to adopt a curious and analytical mindset when evaluating stocks. He suggests considering not only the current market value but also the potential acquisition price by other investors. Price recommends allocating two-thirds of a portfolio to value stocks and dedicating the remaining one-third to special situation instruments like arbitrage and distressed securities.  He cautions against blindly following market trends and emphasizes that investors should focus on opportunities others may overlook, such as mispriced assets.

articles.title: U.P. STF busts SSC exam-rigging racket in Greater Noida; seven held - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) arrested seven individuals in Greater Noida for their involvement in rigging Staff Selection Commission (SSC) online recruitment examinations. The accused allegedly used proxy servers and dummy candidates to manipulate the exams for constables in the CAPF, SSF, and riflemen in the Assam Rifles.  Pradeep Chauhan, a Muzaffarnagar resident who established the online examination center "Balaji Digital Zone," was identified as the alleged mastermind of the racket. The STF recovered ₹50 lakh in cash, electronic devices, and other evidence during the raid. The investigation is ongoing with four other members of the gang still at large.

articles.title: Pakistan steps up airport screening amid Ebola outbreak in Africa - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's health ministry has intensified airport screening measures and directed all provinces to remain on alert following the recent Ebola outbreak in Africa. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) and World Health Organisation’s (WHO) offices in Pakistan are monitoring the situation, while the ministry emphasized that the risk to Pakistan is extremely low due to limited travel links with affected countries.  The ministry also confirmed that it possesses the capacity to diagnose Ebola and has issued directives for preparedness measures.

articles.title: Failing chemical tank forces thousands to evacuate in Southern California | Environment News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Thousands of residents in Southern California have been ordered to evacuate their homes after a storage tank containing hazardous chemicals began to fail. The Orange County Fire Authority and Garden Grove Police Department are working to stabilize the situation, with firefighters attempting to reduce the tank's temperature and prevent it from leaking or exploding.  GKN Aerospace, where the tank is located, has urged residents to evacuate immediately as officials warn that a rupture could create a plume of flammable vapors.

articles.title: Senegal President Faye sacks prime minister Sonko after months or tensions
articles.rephrased_article: President Bassirou Diomaye Faye of Senegal has dismissed Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko and dissolved the government, citing months of tensions between them. The decree followed a parliamentary session where Sonko criticized Faye.  The move comes amid mounting economic pressure in the country, with its public debt exceeding 132% of GDP. Sonko, who enjoys widespread popularity among young Senegalese, has vowed to "sleep with a light heart" despite the dismissal.

articles.title: Board of Peace focus on Hamas risks return to war in Gaza, critics say | Israel-Gaza war | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Nickolay Mladenov, the high representative for Gaza, blamed Hamas for the stalled ceasefire, accusing it of refusing to accept verified decommissioning and relinquish coercive control. However, Hamas rejected these accusations, stating that the report reflects a biased Israeli position and serves as an attempt to justify further escalation. Critics argue that Mladenov's report unfairly blames Hamas, potentially legitimizing Benjamin Netanyahu's potential return to war.  Despite Israel's continued airstrikes and expansion of its control over Gaza, the NCAG, tasked with overseeing disarmament, has been prevented from entering Gaza by Israeli authorities.

articles.title: Stephen Hawking’s father worried his son ‘does not study much’, diaries reveal | Stephen Hawking | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Stephen Hawking, a world-renowned physicist and author of "A Brief History of Time," defied medical expectations after being diagnosed with motor neurone disease at age 21.  His father, Frank Hawking, expressed concerns about his son's future in previously unknown diaries that have been made available to biographer Graham Farmelo. The diaries offer a glimpse into Hawking's formative years and the challenges he faced, including his struggle with his illness and his father's disappointment.  Farmelo's biography, "Hawking," will be published on September 24th by John Murray.

articles.title: Oil prices settle higher on slow progress in US-Iran peace talks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Brent and WTI crude oil futures experienced gains on Friday, driven by shifting expectations for a peace deal between Iran and the U.S.  Diplomatic sources indicated progress in talks, with Pakistan's army chief traveling to Iran, while U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio expressed optimism about potential resolution. However, uncertainties remain regarding Iran's uranium stockpile and control over the Strait of Hormuz, and global oil inventories continue to deplete due to reduced oil flows through the strait.  Analysts predict a modest increase in July production by OPEC+ members, but full oil flow through the strait is not expected until the first or second quarter of 2027.

articles.title: Nagaland intensifies ASF containment measures; pork sale banned in several districts - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Nagaland's government has intensified surveillance and containment measures following the outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF).  Several districts have imposed bans and restrictions on pig imports, transportation, and sales to prevent further spread. The Directorate of Animal Husbandry and Veterinary Services is actively engaged in surveillance, containment, awareness campaigns, sample collection, and bio-security measures.  The ASF outbreak has led to the temporary closure of pork shops in several parts of the state and a significant impact on local consumption patterns and livelihoods for pig farmers and traders.

articles.title: Gilgeous-Alexander leads Thunder past Spurs for 2-1 NBA playoff lead | Basketball News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The Oklahoma City Thunder defeated the San Antonio Spurs 123-108 in Game 3 of their Western Conference Finals series, taking a 2-1 lead.  Shai Gilgeous-Alexander led the Thunder with 26 points while Jared McCain and Jaylin Williams contributed significant bench scoring. The Spurs' early 15-point lead was overcome by the Thunder, who capitalized on strong performances from Gilgeous-Alexander and a dominant second quarter. The intensity of the game escalated in the third quarter with a physical altercation between players, but the Thunder maintained their advantage throughout the fourth to secure the victory.  Game four will be played in San Antonio on Sunday.

articles.title: Rs50,000 fine in Punjab for illegal offal disposal on Eid - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz ordered a Rs50,000 fine for throwing animal waste and offal in streets during Eidul Azha. She directed authorities to remain vigilant at cattle markets and enforce bans on illegal livestock trading, hide collection by banned organizations, loudspeakers use at hide-collection camps, and display of weapons and aerial firing.  Ms Nawaz also emphasized the importance of maintaining ecological balance and ensuring the survival of life on Earth through effective measures for protecting endangered species and conserving the ecosystem.

articles.title: Multimedia arts project wins Sycamore Gap tree commission after public vote | Art and design | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Helix Arts and George King Architects won a public vote to create a "living archive" from preserved wood of the felled Sycamore Gap tree. The project, “The People’s Tree,” will use participatory storytelling, sound, and sculpture to celebrate the beloved sycamore and capture memories of its loss.  It will involve communities across the UK, including those who haven't had access to nature, through interactive elements like a digital archive and co-created artworks. The project is expected to be completed by autumn 2027 and will include the planting of 49 "trees of hope" saplings across the UK.

articles.title: Dollar near six-week high amid Iran war jitters - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Iran's foreign minister met with Pakistan's interior minister to discuss proposals for ending the U.S.-Israeli conflict, according to Iranian media reports.  Traders are concerned about ongoing energy disruptions and their impact on consumer prices, potentially forcing a tighter monetary policy response from the Federal Reserve. The dollar index rose slightly while the yen weakened against the greenback as rising oil prices and persistent inflation pressures continue to affect global markets.

articles.title: Sulur minor girl abduction and murder: Law and order a serious concern in T.N., says Udhayanidhi Stalin - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Udhayanidhi Stalin, leader of the Opposition, expressed concern over 30 major crimes within 12 days of the new government assuming office. These incidents include sexual violence, ganja smuggling, and the abduction and murder of a minor girl in Coimbatore. Stalin called for swift justice for the victim's family and urged the Chief Minister to prioritize law and order to prevent future incidents.

articles.title: Iran war day 85: Tehran says major gaps remain in US talks | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, arrived in Tehran to intensify diplomatic efforts for a US-Iran peace deal. Iranian officials acknowledged significant gaps remain between the two sides despite ongoing talks and emphasized that ending the war is essential for any future agreement.  While Qatar has been praised for supporting Pakistani-led mediation efforts, tensions remain over Iran’s enriched uranium program and control of the Strait of Hormuz. The US continues to engage in diplomatic efforts with Iran, but major differences persist. Meanwhile, escalating violence between Israel and Lebanon has resulted in casualties and strained the Lebanese economy.

articles.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX carries out mostly successful Starship test flight - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: SpaceX successfully conducted a test flight of its Starship spacecraft, which splashed down into the Indian Ocean after a mostly successful journey. The third-generation Starship carried out maneuvers including flipping upright and reigniting its engines despite one malfunctioning during an initial burn. Elon Musk, CEO of SpaceX, praised his team's efforts on X, calling it "epic".  The company is preparing for a potentially record initial public offering in June.

articles.title: Anthony Albanese visibly emotional after defending Labor’s capital gains tax and negative gearing changes | Australian politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Anthony Albanese, the prime minister, defended his government's proposed changes to negative gearing, capital gains tax (CGT), and family trusts. He argued that these reforms are necessary to rebalance the housing market in favor of first-time home buyers and ensure a fairer system for working Australians.  Albanese emphasized that Labor is committed to supporting aspiration for all, including young people who struggle to enter the housing market. While some Labor MPs expressed concerns about the potential negative impact on property investors, Chris Bowen, the energy minister, stated that these changes are crucial for intergenerational equity and acknowledged that they may be controversial but ultimately beneficial.  The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, criticized the budget as an attack on young Australians and a threat to their aspirations.

articles.title: Planning SIPs for a car or house in 10 years? Experts recommend diversified equity funds for long-term goals - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Pankaj Mathpal, MD of Optima Money Managers, advised viewers seeking to invest through SIPs with a 10-year horizon to consider diversified equity funds like ICICI Prudential Midcap Fund, Motilal Oswal Large and Midcap Fund, Bajaj Finserv Flexicap Fund, and HDFC Midcap Fund. He cautioned against investing in gold ETFs due to the government's efforts to reduce gold imports and recommended a focus on diversified mutual funds and multi-asset allocation funds for risk management. Mathpal also warned against excessive exposure to thematic or sectoral funds without understanding market cycles and emphasized that investors with limited knowledge should stick to these strategies.

articles.title: 'Poor thing': Iran mocks Donald Trump as viral buffalo resembling him loses appetite - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Iran shared a viral video of a Bangladeshi albino buffalo resembling Donald Trump, claiming the animal lost its appetite due to comparisons to the US president. The buffalo, named "Donald Trump," has become a popular attraction in Bangladesh ahead of Eid al-Adha.  The US and Israel launched strikes on Iran in February, triggering weeks of escalating tensions between the two countries. Trump met with senior officials to discuss potential military action against Iran if negotiations fail. Diplomatic efforts are underway through Pakistan Army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir's visit to Tehran and a Qatari delegation's arrival in Iran.

articles.title: Uttar Pradesh woman killed by boyfriend after she refuses to accompany him - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ali Mohammad, 25, has been arrested for allegedly strangling his 21-year-old girlfriend, Reshma, inside her home in Uttar Pradesh's Shamli district. The incident occurred on Friday evening, with family members present.  Police say Ali Mohammad attacked Reshma after she refused to accompany him somewhere and both he and his associate, Aliyas, were apprehended at the scene. The body has been sent for a post-mortem examination, and police are continuing their investigation.

articles.title: World Cup 2026: Which star players will miss the tournament? | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Several high-profile players will miss the 2026 World Cup in North America due to injuries or failed qualifying. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, a standout winger for Georgia, won't be at the tournament after his country failed to qualify.  Robert Lewandowski, a veteran striker for Poland, hinted at international retirement following their failure to qualify, while Gianluigi Donnarumma and Sandro Tonali, key players for Italy, will also miss out due to the Azzurri's disappointing qualifying campaign. Victor Osimhen and Ademola Lookman of Nigeria are another notable absence after a shock penalty shootout defeat in the African playoffs.  Hugo Ekitike suffered an Achilles tendon injury, while Estevao and Rodrygo, both from Brazil, were sidelined by hamstring and knee injuries respectively.

articles.title: Rubio starts first visit to India on heels of US-China summit - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio began a four-day visit to India, focusing on strengthening ties with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.  Rubio's first stop was in Kolkata, where he visited the headquarters of Mother Teresa's charity and prayed over her tomb. He then traveled to New Delhi, where he is scheduled to meet with Modi later on Saturday. During his visit, Rubio will also participate in a meeting of foreign ministers from the Quad, a group of democracies seeking to counter China's influence in the Indian Ocean.  The trip comes as President Donald Trump has shifted US priorities and relations with both India and China have become more complex.

articles.title: One dead in NYC's Staten Island after shipyard explosion
articles.rephrased_article: A barge explosion at a Staten Island shipyard on Friday injured over 30 people, including firefighters and first responders.  One civilian died in the incident, which began with reports of workers trapped and a fire. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani declared it a complex emergency situation, prompting additional responders to the scene. The cause of the fire and explosion is under investigation.
